main_text.p: (Sic in Veneto exemplari legitur: at in Basileensi editione, אפתחא דקרתא In porta Urbis, quod synechdochice de Roma intelligendum) & quod est signum ejus? Sedet inter pauperes portantes morbos, id est, leprosos, ut Scholiastes explicat: Hac illic. Pluribus ibidem videtur, quomodo Veteres de Messia, ejus nomine & adventu tempore, fuerint solliciti. Cum verò posteriores Judæi, prioribus illis pejores, animadvertissent, omnes terminos ab Antiquis constitutos præteriisse, neque Messiam, qui illis quidem placeret, venisse, anathemate interdictum, ne quis tempus adventus ejus supputaret, ut paginâ præcedenti ibidem legitur: תפח רוחן של מחשבי קצין Rumpatur spiritus eorum, qui supputant terminos.
ניק Hiph. הניק Lactavit: Fut. ותניקהו Et lactavit eum, Exod.2.9. Convenit cum ינק.
ניר Hiph. הניר Novellavit, Agrum de novo proscidit: Imp. נירו Novellate, Jer.3.4. pro הנירו : Sic Hos. 10.12. Apud Rabbinos, נרה שנה ראשונה Novellat anno primo, & anno secundo serit.
ניר m. Novale, Ibid. & Prov.13.23. Aliam ejus significa-tionem vide in נור.
נכד inasc. Nepos: Et collective, Nepotes, Posteri; Job.18.19. Jes.14.22. Aff. ולנכדי Et nepoti meo; Genes.21. v.23.

נכה Hiph. הכה Percussit, Cæcidit: Metaphoricè, Propagare, Diffundere. Præt. והנה ארץ Et percutiet terram, Jesa.11.4. Futurum, per Apocopam, וירשרשיו Et percutiet radices suas, Hos.14.6: id est, Propagabit, Diffundet. Non dissimilis usus Verbi מכה est. Hiph: Præterit. הוכה Percussus; Cæsus fuit; Psalm.102.5. Particip. Præt. המכה Percussi, Num.25.14. Constr. נכה Jesa.53.4. מכים Cæsi sunt, Cæduntur; Exo.5.16. Constr.

page.notes: Hebrew and Greek are copied from the scan, without vowel points, where none are printed. The large Hebrew headwords (ניק, ניר, נכד, נכה) are set as the opening word of each entry. The running head reads ני נכ, with the first word and the second word printed in different sizes. The catchword חרב is at the bottom right and is not repeated in the text. Printing errors such as "Isaiah" and the s/f forms in the original are kept as printed where legible; Latin long s is written as s here only because it is printed that way on the page.
